question.text: This empire located in the Indian subcontinent was founded by Babur. Shah Jahan who built the Taj Mahal, was a ruler of this empire.
question.clue: In the 18th century, the Bengal War and the Carnatic Wars caused this dynasty to lose territory to France and Great Britain.

swap.text: Meaning "Crown of Palaces", this mausoleum in India was built by Emperor Shah Jahan for his wife, Mumtaz.
swap.clue: A controversy was raised in 2017 when this building was excluded from tourism materials produced in Uttar Pradesh as officials deemed this building's Mughal builders were "traitors."

question.leadin: Identify some countries that gained their independence from Great Britain.
question.text: Muhammad Ali Jinnah served as its first Governor-General after its independence in 1947; the ill-conceived division of Punjab and Bengal with its neighbor, India, caused sectarian riots as Muslims moved to this country.
question.clue: At a 2007 rally, a female leader of this country and daughter of former leader Zulfikar Ali was assassinated at a political rally in Rawalpindi.

swap.leadin: This man achieved his goals using satyagraha, or the force of truth.
swap.text: Name this leader who advocated nonviolence to help India achieve independence. In 1948, he was assassinated by Nathuram Godse.
swap.clue: This this man led a March to Dandi which led to a declaration of Pura Swaraj, or complete self-rule.

question.text: After Pan Am Flight 73 was hijacked on the ground in this country, Gaddafi paid the American victims $150 million. Another act of terrorism saw this country's PM Benazir Bhutto assassinated in 2007.
question.answerHtml: Pakistan [or Islamic Republic of Pakistan or Jamhuryat Islami Pakistan]
question.clue: This country began enriching uranium in response to a neighboring country's Smiling Buddha test.

swap.leadin: Identify these historical people, who all hold the honorary title of 'father of the nation'.
swap.text: This man assumed leadership of his country's National Congress in 1921. His 'salt march'in 1930 emphasised his commitment to non-violent protest against the British Empire.
swap.answerHtml: Mahatma Gandhi [prompt on just Gandhi by asking ‘which one?’]
swap.clue: He promoted swadeshi, the boycott of foreign goods, as part of a campaign to increase use of khadi textiles.
swap.set: 2023 Politics & History with a side of Memes

question.leadin: This organization defeated many of its rivals in the Carnatic wars.
question.text: Name this organization. One mutiny against this organization was caused by the supposed presence of animal grease in the cartridges of the Enfield rifle.
question.answerHtml: British East India Company [or BEIC; accept Honourable East India Company, English East India Company; prompt on East India Company]
question.clue: One representative of this organization, Warren Hastings, reported on a 1770 famine caused by the policies of its official, Robert Clive.

swap.text: This South Asian country also attended the conference. This country's independence movement was led by Mahatma Gandhi.
swap.clue: An ambassador to this country erected the Heliodorus pillar.

question.leadin: Name these nineteenth-century conflicts involving Britain.
question.text: This 1857 revolt in India was allegedly brought on by the cartridges for the new Enfield rifles being greased with pork and beef fat.
question.clue: The notoriously bloody Siege of Cawnpore took place during this event, which was triggered by a new Enfield cartridge that used animal fats as grease, thus offending both Hindus and Muslims.

swap.leadin: In 1962, 15,000 people of Chinese heritage living in this city were sent to prison camps following a border war.
swap.text: Name this city whose Christian minority was served by the Missionaries of Charity, a group whose founder won the 1979 Nobel Peace Prize.
swap.answerHtml: Kolkata [or Calcutta] (The Missionaries of Charity was founded by Mother Teresa.)
swap.clue: Governmental offices from Murshidabad were moved to this city by Warren Hastings.

question.text: A sculpture depicting four of these animals, standing back-to-back and representing the four cardinal directions, originally appeared on the top of the Ashoka pillar at Sarnath.
question.clue: Pairs of these animals that were sculpted with cloth balls under one of their paws often stood at the entrance of imperial Chinese buildings.

swap.leadin: This revolt was partly caused by the introduction of rifle cartridges greased by pig and cow fat.
swap.text: Name this revolt of 1857 in which Indian soldiers rebelled against British officers. The British Raj was formed after this revolt.
swap.answerHtml: Sepoy Revolt [or Sepoy Rebellion or Sepoy Mutiny; prompt on Indian Rebellion of 1857]
swap.clue: Post offices were special targets of one side in this event, which began in the town of Meerut.

question.leadin: A musical automaton of a tiger mauling a European man was discovered in this ruler's capital after its capture by the British.
question.text: Name this "Tiger of Mysore" who, along with his father, resisted the British East India Company in four wars. His defeat at the Battle of Seringapatam ended Mysore's independence.
question.clue: The V&A owns a wooden automaton commissioned by this man of a creature biting into the neck of a Western soldier.

swap.leadin: John Zephaniah Holwell wrote about a prison in this city, describing how 123 people died in one night due to heat exhaustion and cramped conditions.
swap.text: Name this city where Siraj ud-Daulah notoriously imprisoned British POW's.
swap.clue: Sir William Jones founded the Asiatic Society in this city with the support of Warren Hastings.

question.leadin: The Federal Party led a protest outside the Galle Face Green against a prime minister with this surname.
question.text: Give this surname of Solomon, who was assassinated by a Buddhist monk after he signed a pact with the leader of the Federal Party. The first woman to become a prime minister in Asia had this last name.
question.clue: This family of Chandrika Kumaratunga, or CBK. Her father Solomon, known as the "Silver Bell of Asia," was assassinated by a Buddhist monk in 1959, after which, her mother Sirimavo became the world's first female prime minister as chair of the Sri Lanka Freedom Party.

swap.text: Solomon and Sirimavo's daughter Chandrika Kumaratunga was nearly assassinated by this ethnic group's namesake "Tigers," an anti-Sinhalese militant group.
swap.answerHtml: Tamil [or Tamil Tigers; or Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam]
swap.clue: This ethnic group created "singing steps" leading up to one of their three "Great Living" temples; that temple depicted legends associated with 63 "poet-saints" of this ethnicity.

question.leadin: Answer the following about violent events in the lead-up to Indian independence.
question.text: A spate of politically-motivated assassinations followed after Lord Curzon announced this 1905 territory-changing action, which was more limited in scope than a similar 1947 action accompanying Indian independence.
question.answerHtml: Partition of Bengal [accept synonyms, accept descriptive equivalents, like the creation of West and East Bengal]

swap.text: Aw Barkhadle may have also spread Islam to this present-day country. Arabic partially inspired the right-to-left Thaana ("TAH-nuh") script for this country's Dhivehi ("dih-VAY-hee") language.
swap.answerHtml: Maldives [or Republic of Maldives; accept Maldive Islands or Sultanate of Maldives]
swap.clue: In the 20th century, this country was long led by the dictator Maumoon Abdul Gayoom, who sparked civil unrest in 2005 by arresting the main opposition figure, Mohamed Nasheed.

question.leadin: One apocryphal account in this religion's history holds that the sixty-nine-year-old Baba Deep held his severed head on his body while storming a holy city in 1757.
question.text: Name this religion whose members were massacred in the Chhota and Wadda Holocausts, which occurred in 1746 and 1762 at the hands of Lakhpat Rai and Ahmad Shah Abdali.
question.clue: That monarch who followed this religion defeated the Afghan king Zaman Shah to capture Lahore, then declared himself a maharaja.

swap.leadin: This author of Secrets of the Bhagavad Gita worked to awaken political fervor through the newspapers Kesari and The Mahratta.
swap.text: Name this founder of the Indian Home Rule League, a nationalist agitator who signed the Lucknow Pact along with Muhammad Ali Jinnah.
swap.clue: During Curzon's rule, this polymath and president of the Indian Home Rule League proposed a campaign to boycott British goods and stop paying taxes after Curzon partitioned Bengal. This man signed the Lucknow Pact with Mohammad Ali Jinnah.
